These imports match the services and interceptors the controller uses.
market-data.controller.ts: getMarketDataOfMarkets, getMarketDataBySymbol and updateMarketData are all under @Controller('market-data'), so the controller covers one concern.

market-data.controller.ts: getMarketDataBySymbol and updateMarketData both repeat the symbolProfileService.getSymbolProfiles lookup and the `!assetProfile && !isCurrency(getCurrencyFromSymbol(symbol))` 404 check. This is minor duplication inside one file.

market-data.controller.ts: both handlers repeat the ownership check `assetProfile?.userId === this.request.user.id`, but each pairs it with different permissions (readMarketDataOfOwnAssetProfile vs. createMarketDataOfOwnAssetProfile/updateMarketDataOfOwnAssetProfile).
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
Both files serve one concern, the market-data HTTP endpoints. MarketDataModule (market-data.module.ts) only registers MarketDataController and imports the modules for the services the controller injects: AdminModule, MarketDataServiceModule, SymbolModule, SymbolProfileModule and the two transform-data-source interceptor modules. The controller uses Nest's guard, interceptor and permission tools the same way across all three handlers.

One small weakness: getMarketDataBySymbol and updateMarketData repeat the same code to check that the asset profile exists. Each one calls symbolProfileService.getSymbolProfiles, then checks `!assetProfile && !isCurrency(getCurrencyFromSymbol(symbol))` and returns 404 if that holds. They also repeat the ownership check `assetProfile?.userId === this.request.user.id`. Because this repetition sits inside a single controller and the permission sets differ between reading and writing (read vs. create/update), I treat it as a code smell, not an invariant split across files or a bypassed abstraction. A private helper would make it cleaner. No file is unrelated to the concern, and the module does not bypass its own abstractions.
